blocks.html: “Learn at first concentration without effort; transform work into play; make every yoke that you have accepted easy and every burden that you carry light— this counsel, or command, or even warning, however you wish to take it is most serious; this is attested by its original source, namely the words of the Master Himself: “My yoke is easy, and my burden is light.” (Matthew 11:30)”
—~Anonymous (likely Valentin Tomberg) (Meditations on the Tarot, pg.8)

according to tradition, Odin himself was the original designer of Hnefatafl— as well as of dice & runes. (Pennick 32) this would make him quite possible the earliest cited game designer. “setting the game” is an inherently divine act.
many plants came to be first as “sports”; anomalous traits in a region of growth, then splintered off into new breeds

“How art became a sort of civilized substitute for magical games and rituals is the story of the detribalization which came with literacy, art, like games, became a mimetic echo of, and relief from, the old magic of total involvement.”

“Videogames reconfigure the body [around a method of input], and they are experienced through this reconfigured body… videogames attune players… [they] don’t just train their players but prime them to affectively orient themselves to the videogame in a particular way.”
—~Brendan Keogh (A Play of Bodies, pgs.89-90)
the flow state is non-linear; to enter for an instant is to be wholly immersed. an instant of the sublime is and instance of flow

“acknowledging that existence precedes essense, that non-human existence precedes the human - we are holding out for an ethics (way, virtuality) which applies to flows of all matter-energy, an ethics from a belief in the creative materiality of all things, the constantly re-arranging eddies and currents of a ceasless flow of novelty. Creative non-equilibrium in all things— even videogames!”
—~David Kanaga (Structure & Alchemy in New Fractal Playspaces pg.42)
